svg.title: How ArChreator works: from an idea to a tested solution, and a business definition you confirmed

div.div: From an idea to a tested solution — and a business definition you confirmed

div.b: 2 · Refine the definition ↻ as many rounds as it takes

div.div: Say the idea, a requirement or a problem, in plain words
Answer the question, or correct what you read
Review and merge the pull request

Walk the layers, top down:
0 Business design · 1 Strategy
2 Business · 3 Information
Preview, in the conversation: what changed about your business, every call taken for you, one question or none
Stop, surfaced to you: it contradicts a decision, reads two ways, or needs your authorization
Scope document, and the register: each component, what it serves, its specification, its code
Your principles and business rules, carried into the framework's standing file
Validators: links, model, prose. End-to-end brief, and a PDF

Spec Kit · OpenSpec · Kiro · BMAD · arc42 or C4
The technical description, and a specification per component owed back to the register
Build the code and its tests, run them, open the pull request

Key deliverable — your strategic and business definition
Who you serve, what you offer, who does what and with which information. Plain Markdown in your repository, confirmed by you, and still true after every change

The implemented and tested solution
Built from the definition, with its technical architecture described end to end
